clue.text: Competitor taking time getting to church door

indicators.note: getting to says the church comes next, reached after the first part
taking here means taking away, so a letter is removed from the competitor

parts.note: an entrant is someone competing in an event
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A runner arrives at a church door just in time, perhaps for a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking time' looks like hurrying, but it means taking T away from ENTRANT, leaving ENTRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is a way in, the point through which one enters a building.

clue.text: Provoke former partner to name names

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to cite is to name or quote as evidence

explanation.surface: Goading an ex into naming people involved.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite feelings is to stir them up, to provoke them.

clue.text: Nuts put TV upside down

indicators.note: upside down in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to set is to put
a TV is a set

explanation.surface: Crazy people hanging the television upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for testicles.

clue.text: Alabama gun scare

parts.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama
a firearm is an arm

explanation.surface: A firearms panic in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a fright or sudden fear, a scare.

clue.text: School group one caught going to Derby perhaps

parts.note: a class is a group of pupils
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A school party catches a bus to Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is not the city but the horse race, one of Britain's five Classics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is one of the English Classic flat races, so an example.

clue.text: Enjoys terrine containing seafood

indicators.note: the words enjoys terrine contain the letters within them, spanning the word break

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a pâté that has shellfish in it.
explanation.definitionFit: This bivalve is a classic item of seafood, often eaten raw.

clue.text: Doctor chats with many a sailor

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A GP chatting with plenty of sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sails a yacht is a type of sailor.

clue.text: Number of exercises said to produce curls

indicators.note: said tells us the phrase is spoken aloud

parts.note: ten is a number and drills are exercises

explanation.surface: A workout routine meant to give someone curly hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendrils are curling shoots of a plant, or wisps of hair, so curls.

clue.text: Disturbed person ingesting drugs makes comeback

indicators.note: ingesting means swallowing, so the drugs go inside
disturbed means the letters are shaken up

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so ES is drugs

explanation.surface: A troubled addict stages a return.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a drug user, but 'Disturbed' is the anagram signal (giving RPONSE) and 'ingesting' the container signal; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A comeback is a retort, a reply or response.

clue.text: Rejected players playing at rival's ground

parts.note: the cast of a play are its players
a team playing at its rival's ground is playing away

explanation.surface: A sports report about dropped players in an away fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown out or discarded can be called a castaway, an outcast that has been rejected.

clue.text: Special educational needs involving constant and regularly messy episodes

indicators.note: involving means the needs abbreviation wraps round the constant

parts.note: SEN is the British abbreviation for special educational needs in schools
C is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter of messy

explanation.surface: A school report about children with special needs causing chaotic incidents.
explanation.walkthrough: Special educational needs is a British school term; 'involving' wraps it round the constant, and 'regularly' takes every other letter of 'messy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenes are incidents or episodes, as in a play or a public row.

clue.text: Upright attitude suddenly adopted when employed

indicators.note: Upright says the hidden letters are read backwards
adopted means the letters are taken up within the words attitude suddenly

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sudden change of posture to stand straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'adopted when employed' as the definition, leaving no hidden indicator; 'adopted' signals the hidden word, 'when' is a link, and 'employed' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something employed has been put to use, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Almost at that place Old Testament figure built vessels

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the place word is dropped

parts.note: there means at that place
Moses is the lawgiver of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A Bible scene: Noah-like, an Old Testament figure built vessels nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' is a link word; the vessels suggest arks but are flasks.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacuum flasks are vessels for keeping drinks hot or cold.

clue.text: Fish losing tail in part of engine

indicators.note: losing tail means the final letter of the fish is cut off

parts.note: a turbot is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A fish loses its tail in machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbocharger, an engine component, is commonly shortened to this word.

clue.text: Great and exciting performance influencing current leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A review praising a thrilling show that shapes modern trends.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective means grand or impressive in scale, so great.

clue.text: Blank stare of female in contest following provocation

indicators.note: following means the contest part comes after the provocation

parts.note: a poke is a prod, a provocation

indicators.note: in means the female goes inside the contest

parts.note: a race is a contest

explanation.surface: A woman in a competition stares blankly after being goaded.
explanation.definitionFit: An expressionless face that reveals nothing, as a card player keeps, is a blank stare.

clue.text: Smiles as stupid request almost succeeded

parts.note: dim means stupid

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the request is dropped

parts.note: a plea is a request
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone grins because a foolish appeal nearly worked.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimples are the small hollows in the cheeks that show when someone smiles, so they stand in for smiles.

clue.text: Advice he disseminated got intended result

indicators.note: disseminated means scattered, so the letters are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: His advice, once spread around, worked.
explanation.definitionFit: To have achieved something is to have reached the goal you set out for.

clue.text: Five éclairs possibly contributing to something felt in gut

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: possibly signals the pastries are rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: Eating five cream pastries leads to a stomach ache.
explanation.definitionFit: Visceral means instinctive, relating to deep bodily feelings in the innards.

clue.text: Insect mound found during time in France

indicators.note: found during means the mound sits inside the time abbreviation

parts.note: CET is Central European Time, the time zone used in France
a rick is a stack or mound of hay

explanation.surface: A bug discovered on a heap while on holiday in France.
explanation.walkthrough: CET is Central European Time, which France keeps.
explanation.definitionFit: This chirping grasshopper relative is an insect.

clue.text: Book classic Chuckle Brothers routine

definitions.meaning: the British comedy duo's catchphrase '..., to you' as they passed objects back and forth

explanation.surface: A book about a famous comedy double act's routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chuckle Brothers were a British children's TV comedy duo famous for 'To me, to you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a weighty volume, and read as two words it is half the duo's catchphrase.

clue.text: Inclination to hypocrisy

explanation.surface: A tendency towards being two-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a slope or tilt and pious, insincere talk.

clue.text: Charlie plays unusual love ballad

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: unusual means the letters appear in a strange order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Charlie performs an odd romantic song.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean song, a kind of narrative ballad.

clue.text: Kind journalist equipped with drugs

parts.note: a sort is a kind
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A friendly reporter carrying narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, being sorted means supplied with drugs.

clue.text: Leader of coup deposing prince and extortionist

indicators.note: deposing means removing, so the prince is taken out

parts.note: a usurper seizes power, as the leader of a coup does

explanation.surface: A coup leader overthrows a prince and a blackmailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of coup' tempts a first-letter pick (C), but it is the whole word USURPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging extortionate interest is an extortionist.

clue.text: Provoke semi-emaciated mongrel

indicators.note: semi- means only half of the word for emaciated is kept

parts.note: thin means emaciated
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Teasing a half-starved stray dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur blame or anger is to bring it on yourself, to provoke it.

clue.text: Sweet made by Bake Off participant causing offence

parts.note: Mel Giedroyc co-presented The Great British Bake Off
odious means hateful, causing offence

explanation.surface: A pudding made by a baking-show contestant that offends the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great British Bake Off is a TV baking contest; Mel Giedroyc was a presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodious means tuneful, and sweet can describe pleasing sounds.

clue.text: Doctor with digestive complaint goes to bits

parts.note: IBS is irritable bowel syndrome

explanation.surface: A doctor with a stomach problem falls to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Dribs, as in dribs and drabs, are small amounts or bits.

clue.text: Vicar returning to black tie event missing last bit of speech

indicators.note: returning means the vicar's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title

indicators.note: missing last bit means the final letter of the event is dropped

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance where black tie is worn

explanation.surface: A clergyman going back to a formal dinner dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbal means spoken, relating to words or speech.

clue.text: You might find her on the fast track?

definitions.text: You might find her on the fast track?

parts.words: You might find her on the fast track?
parts.note: the fast track suggests an ambitious career, but literally it is a running track for short races

explanation.surface: An ambitious woman whose career is on the fast track.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-distance runner competes on the track at top speed.

clue.text: Boring model sounds sweet

indicators.note: sounds says the phrase is spoken aloud

parts.note: dull means boring and to sit is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A tedious fashion model has a pleasant voice.
explanation.walkthrough: DULL SIT, said aloud, matches the British pronunciation of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulcet tones are soft and pleasing, sweet to the ear.

clue.text: Reflect on society consumed by alcohol

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the drink

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: Musing about a society ruined by drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider is to think carefully, to reflect.
